questions.question: What is contraception? Explain how a condom prevents pregnancy and infection, and give three rules for using a condom correctly.
questions.expected_answer: Contraception is any method used to prevent pregnancy. A condom is a thin latex sheath that collects semen so sperm cannot reach the egg, and forms a barrier that stops the exchange of body fluids, reducing the risk of STIs including HIV. Rules: check the expiry date and wrapper for damage; open carefully without teeth or scissors; put it on before any sexual contact; pinch the tip to remove air; use only water-based lubricants, never oil-based products; use a new condom every time; hold it at the base when withdrawing and dispose of it properly.

questions.question: Distinguish between HIV and AIDS. State three ways HIV is transmitted and three ways it is not transmitted.
questions.expected_answer: HIV is the human immunodeficiency virus, which attacks CD4 white blood cells of the immune system. AIDS is the late stage of untreated HIV infection, when the immune system is so weakened that the body cannot fight infections such as TB. Transmitted by: unprotected sexual intercourse; sharing needles or sharp objects contaminated with blood; from mother to baby during pregnancy, birth or breastfeeding without treatment. Not transmitted by: hugging or shaking hands; sharing cups, plates or toilets; swimming pools; coughing, sneezing, sweat or tears; mosquito bites.

questions.question: Describe three consequences of early sexual activity and explain why someone who looks healthy should still be tested.
questions.expected_answer: Physical: unplanned pregnancy, with higher risks for a young mother's body; STIs including HIV. Emotional: regret, anxiety, pressure and damaged self-esteem. Social and educational: many pregnant teenagers leave school, which limits future opportunities; responsibilities of parenthood before being ready. Legal: the age of consent is 16. Many STIs, including HIV, have no symptoms for a long time, so a person can be infected and pass it on without knowing; testing is the only way to know one's status.
